name: Domaine des Sénéchaux Châteauneuf-du-Pape 2016
text:
## Domaine des Sénéchaux Châteauneuf-du-Pape 2016

**The story.** Domaine des Sénéchaux, dating from the 14th century, is among the oldest wineries in [Châteauneuf-du-Pape](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Domaine+des+S%C3%A9n%C3%A9chaux,+Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape,+France&t=k), named for one of its main plots in the "Bois Sénéchaux" neighbourhood. Its wines are distributed by J.M. Cazes Sélection ([J.M. Cazes Sélection, technical sheet](https://www.jmcazes.com/sites/default/files/upload/vintage/pdf/2016_-_domaine_des_senechaux_rouge_-_uk.pdf)).

**The vineyards.** The plots, covered in quartzite pebbles and facing south-west, sit on three kinds of subsoil: 8 hectares of stony limestone-clay slopes, 11 hectares of molasse and *safre* (sandy limestone) and 3 hectares of deep sand ([J.M. Cazes Sélection](https://www.jmcazes.com/sites/default/files/upload/vintage/pdf/2016_-_domaine_des_senechaux_rouge_-_uk.pdf)).

**The wine.** The 2016 is 60% [Grenache](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenache), 22% [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), 17% [Mourvèdre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mourv%C3%A8dre) and 1% other varieties, macerated 29 to 35 days and aged 15 months: 25% in once-used barrels, 53% in casks and 22% in vats; 15% alcohol. The estate's note: dazzling garnet, candied morello cherry, ripe berries and delicate spice; a powerful attack, jammy red and dark berries, pepper and an elegant, lightly oaked finish ([J.M. Cazes Sélection](https://www.jmcazes.com/sites/default/files/upload/vintage/pdf/2016_-_domaine_des_senechaux_rouge_-_uk.pdf)).

**The vintage.** 2016 is one of the great modern years in the southern Rhône. [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/southern-rhone) quotes [Michel Chapoutier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapoutier) saying it could be better than the legendary 1990: warm conditions and reduced yields gave wines of great concentration, "certainly one of the great vintages" for reds, and safe for cellaring into the 2030s. The estate describes a mild, dry winter and spring, a hot, dry summer, then mid-September rain and the drying [mistral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistral_%28wind%29): "very promising".

**What the critics say for 2016.** As listed on the estate's [technical sheet](https://www.jmcazes.com/sites/default/files/upload/vintage/pdf/2016_-_domaine_des_senechaux_rouge_-_uk.pdf):
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck): 95** (August 2018).
- **Jeff Leve, The Wine Cellar Insider: 93** (2018).
- **[Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson): 17+/20** (December 2016).
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 91.4** (from your CellarTracker list).
- (The sheet lists scores but not the critics' notes.)

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is ten years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2026 to 2031. So it is just entering its window: kirsch, dark berries, pepper and spice. Decant an hour ahead.

**Food.** Roast lamb with thyme, a Provençal daube, duck with olives, or a mushroom ragout.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Sénéchaux at the moment.

**From the history books**
- **The popes and their castle.** In 1309 [Pope Clement V](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Clement_V) moved the papacy to [Avignon](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Palais+des+Papes,+Avignon,+France&t=k); his successor [John XXII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_XXII) built the summer castle that gave Châteauneuf-du-Pape, "the Pope's new castle", its name ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
- **France's first appellation.** Local growers led by Baron [Pierre Le Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Le_Roy_de_Boiseaumari%C3%A9) of [Château Fortia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teau_Fortia) drew up France's first [appellation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appellation_d'origine_contr%C3%B4l%C3%A9e) rules in 1923, made law in 1936 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).

**Curious details**
- **The flying-cigar law.** In 1954, after local reports of [UFOs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flying_saucer), the Châteauneuf council banned "flying cigars" from flying over or landing in the commune; the decree is still in force ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ch%C3%A2teauneuf-du-Pape_AOC)).
